editorial:
Imagine being a young guy who has everything figured out in his head but nothing figured out in real life. That is exactly who you meet in this story. You follow Floyd, a stylish Belgrade dandy who spends his days dodging the army and ignoring his girlfriend. All he cares about is his small rally car and the dream of moving up to a bigger racing class. The vibe is a mix of funny and stressful, as you watch him pretend that adult responsibilities just do not exist. It feels like a snapshot of youth where the only thing that matters is the next big race on Saturday.

What really works here is how the movie captures that feeling of being stuck between being a kid and a man. The acting is natural, and the racing scenes add a nice spark of energy. While the pacing slows down a bit in the middle, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy character studies with a bit of humor, you will love this. Since this is an older gem, you should try to find the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture. If you prefer streaming, check if it is available for rent on Apple TV to see those vintage cars in high definition.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head during the big race. Floyd pushes himself to the limit, but the movie shows that you cannot run away from reality forever. He does not get the fairy tale ending he expected. Instead, he is forced to face the consequences of his laziness and the people he hurt. He realizes that his obsession with the race was just a way to avoid growing up, leaving you with a bittersweet feeling.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves coming-of-age stories and vintage cars.
